chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'From where is the cutting obligated?' So he extended his fingers and said, 'From here,' meaning from the hinge of the palm.

key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: The act of cutting, specifically referring to the hadd punishment for theft.
key_terms.مَفْصِلُ الْكَفِّ: The hinge or joint of the palm, referring to the wrist area where the hand meets the forearm.

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should the hand be cut according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise anatomical boundary for the hadd punishment of theft by pointing to the wrist joint (mafsil al-kaff). This definition is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for ensuring the penalty is applied correctly, distinguishing the wrist from the forearm or the palm itself. The hadith underscores the importance of specific physical markers in implementing divine law with precision.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘From where is the cutting (of the hand) Obligated?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> extended his fingers and said: ‘For over here, meaning from the hinge of the palm’.
